speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I must correct that previous assessment; Tuberculosis is extremely unlikely in a 33-week preterm infant presenting with acute distress just two hours after birth. Given the prematurity and classic signs like grunting and retractions, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of Hyaline Membrane Disease, also known as Respiratory Distress Syndrome. Please provide the results of the Chest X-Ray and Arterial Blood Gas tests to confirm.
